learning_outcomes.text: Students will know: current topics in the organization and management of production factors, together with quantitative methodologies for profitability analysis and for the optimisation of production factors.
Students will know: the broader multidisciplinary context of engineering, with a focus on problem solving, starting from the problem to identify its causes and possible countermeasures.
Students will know: the techniques and methods applicable to plant and industrial logistics design — demand forecasting, layout study, warehouse sizing — together with their limitations.
Students will know: the non-technical implications of engineering practice, including the economic and safety implications of plant design choices.
Students will be able to: select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods for the production of goods and services, such as material handling, storage and identification systems.
Students will be able to: combine theory and practice to solve multidisciplinary plant design and management problems, taking into account both technical and non-technical constraints.

Students will develop the ability to work collaboratively and effectively within a team, understanding the context of plant engineering problems and recognizing their main interdisciplinary implications.
Students will be able to communicate information, problems and solutions in the field of industrial plants to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, using appropriate technical language.
Students will be able to graphically represent and communicate technical data, results and solutions through diagrams, graphs and tables.
Students will be able to identify and consult bibliographic sources and technical documentation (manuals, databases, digital resources), selecting relevant information.

Students will be able to understand and interpret the fundamental principles of design, production and maintenance processes, operating in compliance with quality, safety and reliability requirements and with reference to the main technical standards.

assessment_rules: The assessment is based on a written assignment consisting of 10 questions of three types: simple theoretical (relative weight 1), theoretical of average difficulty (relative weight 2), and articulated exercises (relative weight 3). To pass, students must have good knowledge of the subject and be able to model an industrial engineering problem. To obtain a high mark, knowledge must be very good and comprehensive. The highest grade with honors requires outstanding ability to manage time, producing an excellent result quickly.
